gf2.revision_kind: git commit (informational navigation metadata; the receipts pin these files by content digest)

lane-enumeration.why: Every implementation of the 64x64 block contract is a variant here, so the family the campaign measures is the family the library publishes.

lane-entry-point.why: The one way to reach a specific lane. A candidate arm names its lane here rather than through a private entry point of its own.

lane-feature-gate.why: An AVX2 lane is published only after the runtime feature test, which is the whole safety contract of each unsafe kernel.

production-preference.why: The order `detect` resolves the production lane in. Adopting a lane is an edit to this constant and to nothing else.

detect-resolves-preference.why: The dispatch every production consumer reaches; the campaign's baseline arm calls it.

ymm6-kernel.why: The candidate that runs all six stages in YMM registers and declares no stack scratch.

movemask-kernel.why: The movemask candidate. Its byte transpose is the tile assembly and its bit-plane extraction the packing that the 32x8 geometry needs to answer the same 64x64 contract, so both are inside every cell that times it.

pshufb-kernel.why: The PSHUFB candidate the issue names.

incumbent-declares-scratch.why: The incumbent lane's declared 512-byte local. Its frame traffic is an intentional scratch, not a compiler spill.

movemask-declares-planes.why: The movemask lane's declared byte-plane array, the second intentional scratch of the family.

asm-incumbent-block-copy.why: The incumbent lane copies the block into its declared local and back out; the annotation counts both calls from the disassembly itself.

asm-ymm6-no-block-copy.why: The candidate copies no block. Its remaining frame traffic belongs to no declared buffer, so it is register pressure rather than scratch.

matrix-transpose-driver.why: The tiling driver of `BitMatrix::transpose` with its block primitive as an argument. The whole-matrix cells drive the production tiling, output allocation, zero padding and tail mask through it.

matrix-transpose-delegates.why: `BitMatrix::transpose` is that driver at the resolved kernel, so a cell and the production entry point run the same code.

bch-bundle-transpose-field.why: The bit-sliced BCH bundle reaches the transpose through this field, which is what a conversion cell substitutes a lane into.

bch-bundle-uses-dispatch.why: The accelerated bundle takes the production dispatch's lane rather than a second wrapper around the same kernel.

absorb-block-transposes.why: The packing half of the conversion: one block transpose bit-slices a lane group's message window before the recurrence consumes it.

unpack-parity-transposes.why: The unpacking half: one block transpose per parity word reads the reduced register back as packed per-frame parity.

bitslice-family-admission.why: The bit-sliced family is admitted by the active profile's minimum batch. The whole-consumer control calls the family entry point directly, so it measures that family whatever the profile admits.

bitslice-min-batch-conservative.why: Under the conservative profile no batch length selects the bit-sliced family, so the consumer the conversion sits inside is reached by installing a profile or by naming the family, not by the default walk.

arm-selects-lane-by-environment.why: One executable serves every arm; the lane is the only difference between a baseline and a candidate child.

arm-baseline-is-production-dispatch.why: The baseline arm runs whatever `detect` publishes, so it is the pinned pre-change implementation rather than a lane named to imitate it.

arm-warm-pass.why: The declared warm policy: one untimed pass of the timed body over every bank, before calibration, in both arms.

arm-control-reports-dispatched-lane.why: The whole-consumer control reports the dispatched lane whatever the arm names, which is what makes it an identity control.
